01

A clear first step

New prescription activation

All services ↑

A new prescription sent by your provider may still need to be activated before a military pharmacy prepares it. Check the current process using the official BAMC pharmacy information or call the pharmacy before making a trip. This website’s visit request form does not activate or transmit a prescription.

Have your question ready and explain whether your provider has already sent the prescription. The pharmacy can tell you what to do next and whether it can fill the medication. Keep prescription documents, identification numbers and health information within the official pharmacy channels.

Before you contact the pharmacy

  • Check whether your provider has sent the prescription.
  • Use the official activation instructions for the pharmacy location.
  • Wait for the pharmacy’s readiness information before traveling.

Prescription processing and website visit requests are separate. A visit confirmation does not mean a medication is ready.

Call (210) 295-9371 TRICARE: military pharmacy prescriptions ↗
02

Plan your next supply

Prescription refills

All services ↑

For a prescription with refills remaining, follow the refill instructions on the label or use the MHS GENESIS Patient Portal when the prescription is available there. The official pharmacy information explains local options. Q-Anywhere is for new prescription activation rather than routine refill requests.

If the prescription has expired or has no refills left, contact the prescriber about a renewal. Allow the processing time advised by the pharmacy. Before collecting, check the pickup location and any readiness notification so that your journey is useful.

A useful refill checklist

  • Check the label and the number of refills remaining.
  • Confirm the pickup location through the official refill channel.
  • Ask the prescriber about an expired prescription or a renewal.

This website does not process refills, renewals or prescription transfers.

Call (210) 295-9371 TRICARE: activation and refill guidance ↗
03

Arrive with a clearer plan

Pickup & collection questions

All services ↑

The Google Maps listing places this pharmacy at the Fort Sam Houston Exchange on Winfield Scott Road. Call the listed pharmacy number with questions about collection and current arrangements. A preferred visit time submitted on this website does not reserve a prescription or guarantee a waiting time.

If someone will collect for you, ask the pharmacy about its current identification and authorization requirements. BAMC also publishes information about ScriptCenter pickup options and their limitations. Confirm which location and method applies to your prescription rather than assuming every item can use a kiosk.

Before setting out

  • Check that the pharmacy has told you the prescription is ready.
  • Confirm the collection location and required identification.
  • Ask about collecting on someone else’s behalf before traveling.

Listed hours can change on federal holidays. Call ahead for special access or pickup arrangements.

Call (210) 295-9371 BAMC: pharmacy locations and pickup information ↗
04

Use the right official information

Eligibility & pharmacy benefits

All services ↑

Military pharmacy services are for eligible beneficiaries. TRICARE provides the official information about eligibility and pharmacy coverage. Check your own circumstances through the appropriate official channel before relying on a service or making a special trip.

Ask what identification is required for collection and whether any installation access arrangements apply to your visit. The website form does not establish eligibility, register a beneficiary or replace a pharmacy check. Never enter a DoD ID number, Social Security number, insurance identifier or medical record into the visit or review forms.

Questions to check in advance

  • Which pharmacy benefits and eligibility rules apply to me?
  • What identification must I bring for collection?
  • Do I need to confirm access arrangements before visiting?

The pharmacy and official TRICARE channels determine service arrangements; submitting a website form does not establish eligibility.

Call (210) 295-9371 TRICARE: eligibility information ↗
05

Make room for your questions

Medication questions & safe disposal

All services ↑

If you are unsure about a medication label or the information supplied with a prescription, ask the pharmacist to explain it. Write down the questions you want to cover and bring the packaging or an up-to-date medication list to the conversation. Discuss personal health information directly with the healthcare team.

For unwanted or expired medication, the FDA recommends looking for a drug take-back option first. Ask the pharmacy which local disposal arrangements are currently available. Needles, sharps and other specialist items may require a different service. Do not assume this location accepts every type of return.

Prepare for the conversation

  • Bring the packaging or a current medication list.
  • Note the instructions or questions you want clarified.
  • Call before bringing unwanted medication or specialist waste.

The website provides general service information and does not give individual treatment or dosing advice.

Call (210) 295-9371 FDA: unused medication disposal ↗
